scope: One six-request comparison from the azuki host; no additional curl probes.
timing_units: seconds; dns/connect/tls/ttfb are cumulative from request start, total includes body transfer
asset_selection: Existing /assets/*.js script URL read from the origin homepage; exactly the same asset requested on the public hostname.

netcheck.derp_latency: Unavailable in the retained summary; the extraction did not return recognized NearestDERP/DERPLatency fields. This does not establish absence of a reachable relay.

static_source_configuration.cache_control: All responses receive Cache-Control: no-store from local_session middleware, including static assets.
static_source_configuration.serving: Existing frontend files are served through StreamingResponse, with no explicit static ETag, Last-Modified, immutable or max-age implementation in this route.
static_source_configuration.runtime_compression_verification: Not measured: these six curl calls did not send Accept-Encoding and did not capture response headers.
static_source_configuration.browser_payload_limit: 304091 bytes is this curl sample's downloaded asset body, not evidence of a browser's compressed transfer size.

conclusions: All six requests returned HTTP 200. Origin total time was 2.2-8.5 ms; public homepage and health were about 203-206 ms during this sample.
The public asset request took 4.481 s: TLS completed at 0.907 s, first byte at 1.146 s, and the remaining body transfer took 3.336 s.
This sample does not support a persistent 6-8 s application-processing delay. Most observed asset delay was outside the local origin response.
A SPA can remain visually empty while its entry script arrives, but this curl test did not measure browser execution or prove the cause of the earlier Chrome blank DOM.
One remote-host sample does not establish every visitor route, the exact relay used, or the cause of intermittent TLS latency. The Mac proxy route is separate.
Gzip support already exists in source. No-store means repeat visits cannot rely on persistent HTTP caching for static assets under the current middleware.
modifications: Only this public report was written; no app, network, process or browser settings changed.
